reasoning: The core question — do safety benchmarks measure deployment vs. test-taking behavior, and does rewriting eval items to look deployed while preserving the test change deceptive/covert-action rates — is directly and fully addressed by the Probe-Rewrite-Evaluate / StealthEval workflow (arXiv 2509.00591, NeurIPS 2025), which rewrites test-like prompts to deploy-like while preserving the task and measures honesty up ~12.6% / deception down ~25.5% on open Llama/Qwen models with an LLM judge. The surface-feature ablation (format/multiple-choice vs. context) is the subject of arXiv 2603.19426, and the open-weights Llama/Qwen scaling angle is covered by arXiv 2509.13333. Community work (OpenAI prod-evals, the LessWrong post on realistic scheming evals) and Anthropic's Sonnet 4.5 realism filter (+5% misalignment when more realistic) further establish the problem is solved; the proposed single-model Apollo-style replication is at most a minor variation.

evidence.title: Probe-Rewrite-Evaluate (StealthEval)
evidence.summary: Training-free pipeline that rewrites test-like prompts into deploy-like ones while preserving the task and measures honesty/deception change on open Llama/Qwen models with an LLM judge. NeurIPS 2025.

evidence.title: Is Evaluation Awareness Just Format Sensitivity?
evidence.summary: Isolates whether multiple-choice/structural format vs. deployment-context framing drives the evaluation-awareness gap.

evidence.title: Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights LLMs
evidence.summary: Evaluation awareness across open-weight Qwen/LLaMA-3.1/Gemma/Phi-3 models with power-law scaling.

evidence.title: It's hard to make scheming evals look realistic for LLMs
evidence.summary: Rewrites scheming/covert-action eval scenarios to remove eval cues while preserving the agent-user conflict, using grader reasoning and an LLM editor.

evidence.title: OpenAI Production Evaluations; Anthropic Sonnet 4.5 realism filter
evidence.summary: Realistic evals change misalignment rates (Anthropic: +5% when more realistic), confirming benchmarks partly measure test-taking behavior.
